clue.text: Appreciating 60 minutes without husband in bar

indicators.note: 'in' places the shortened time period inside the word for bar

parts.note: 'saving' as a preposition means except, like 'bar'

indicators.note: 'without' tells us to go without, dropping that letter from the time period

parts.note: sixty minutes make an hour
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone enjoying an hour in the pub with the husband left at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like the pub in the surface, but it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Savouring something means relishing it and taking pleasure in it slowly, a close synonym of appreciating.

clue.text: Cane comedian in school

indicators.note: 'in' places the comedian inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: a standard abbreviation for school
a wit is a funny person, a joker

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned story of a class clown being caned at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is a thin flexible stick used for beating, much like a cane; both nouns and verbs work.

clue.text: Even a Times cryptic can be a foreign language

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so the letters before it are to be rearranged into something else

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A wry remark that even the famously hard Times crossword can read like a foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnamese is the national tongue spoken in Vietnam, an example of a language that is foreign to English speakers.

clue.text: Furious engineer ruins map

indicators.note: to engineer something is to construct or contrive it, so the following letters are rebuilt

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An angry engineer has spoilt a map, picturing a workplace row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a noun, the furious person, but it is a verb telling you to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up in arms is an idiom for being angrily protesting, strongly indignant about something.

clue.text: Arrange to be at home with family

parts.note: someone at home is in
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Making plans to spend time at home with relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: To ink in an appointment is to confirm it firmly in a diary, as opposed to pencilling it, so to fix or settle it.

clue.text: Lech organised church dance music

parts.note: a lecher is called an old goat
to run an event is to organise it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A lecherous man set up a dance in the church hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' looks like an anagram signal but gives a word in its own right; Goa trance is a genre named after the Indian state of Goa.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa trance is a style of electronic dance music that grew from beach parties in Goa in the 1990s.

clue.text: Nonentity turned over photo with woman

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the word for photo is read from its end

parts.note: pic is short for picture
her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A dull man turned over a picture of a woman, perhaps in a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher can mean a person of no importance or influence, just as a zero has no value.

clue.text: Scum is a movie

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a thin layer on a surface

explanation.walkthrough: Scum is also the title of a notorious 1979 British borstal film, so the surface reads as a true statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A film is both a thin coating such as scum on a pond and a motion picture shown at the cinema.

clue.text: Dealing with Louise's travel companion Mike moving south and running away

indicators.note: in a down entry, south is downward, so that letter leaves its place and goes to the bottom

parts.note: on means about or concerning
the film Thelma and Louise follows two women on the road
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A road-trip tale where friends are fleeing the law, as in the film.
explanation.walkthrough: Thelma and Louise is a 1991 film about two women on the run; the Mike in the name drops to the bottom of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: On the lam is American slang for fleeing, especially escaping from the police or justice.

clue.text: Wishing to be free from restrictions, one is charged for belief

indicators.note: the restrictions are the bounding letters at each end, which are to be freed off

parts.note: hoping means wishing
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: Someone wanting liberty is charged with a crime because of their beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: HOPING loses its first and last letters to leave OPIN, followed by ION.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or judgement held by someone, close in sense to a belief they hold.

clue.text: Failing to shake off Victor, choose mountaineering equipment

indicators.note: shaking something off gets rid of it, so that letter is lost from the word for failing

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing
Victor is V in the NATO alphabet
to pick is to choose

explanation.surface: A climber who cannot shake off a rival called Victor picks gear.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice pick, or ice axe, is a climber's tool for cutting holds and gripping frozen slopes.

clue.text: I'm doubtful sleeping policeman needs hotel

parts.note: a sleeping policeman is British slang for a speed bump in the road
Hotel is H in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A sceptical remark about whether a speed bump really needs a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeping policeman is the British name for a speed bump, a raised hump across the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Humph is an interjection expressing scepticism or disbelief, the sound a doubtful person makes.

clue.text: Exciting new erotica includes introduction from Noddy Holder

indicators.note: includes means the following letter is taken inside the earlier words
exciting means stirring up, so the gathered letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of Noddy

explanation.surface: Racy new material includes something from Noddy Holder, the Slade singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Noddy Holder fronted the glam rock band Slade; 'Holder' looks like part of his name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A container is anything that holds something else, such as a box, jar or tin.

clue.text: Can lose oar at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A rower may drop an oar while out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb 'is able to' but is the noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised spray can, so the noun can stands for it.

clue.text: Temporary withholding of dodgy payment by government

parts.note: sus is informal for suspicious or dodgy
the state pension is a regular payment from government

explanation.surface: A suspicious state payment being frozen while it is investigated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' looks like an anagram signal but gives the slang word SUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspension is a temporary halt or stopping, such as the suspension of benefits or pay.

clue.text: Lodger is very boring chap

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the word for very pierces the word for chap

parts.note: a chap is a man
so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: A complaint that the person renting a room is tedious company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodger' is not a tenant but a member of a lodge, the meeting group of Freemasons.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freemason belongs to a Masonic lodge, so the setter calls him a lodge member, a 'Lodger'.

clue.text: Valley with large mammals upset animal carer

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the whole sequence reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a dale is a valley
L is the abbreviation for large
bats are flying mammals

explanation.surface: A valley full of big beasts has disturbed someone who looks after animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable lad is someone employed to look after horses in a racing stable, a kind of animal keeper.

clue.text: Perhaps Trump followed by small crowd

parts.note: Trump is an example of a president, abbreviated PRES
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Donald Trump followed around by a little crowd of supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a dense throng of people pushing together, as in the press of the crowd.

clue.text: River Wear damaged politician's audio equipment

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so those letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: The River Wear in north-east England flooded and wrecked an MP's hi-fi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Wear' reads as one name, the Durham river, but River gives a different river and Wear is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A power amp is the amplifier stage that drives loudspeakers, a piece of sound equipment.

clue.text: Like to meet American uncle in Indian region

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
Uncle Sam personifies the United States

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to meet their uncle from the USA in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a state of north-east India famous for its tea plantations.

clue.text: Briefly recommend drinking a drink

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the shortened word swallows the following letter
briefly means cut short, so the word for recommend loses its final letter

parts.note: to advocate is to recommend
taken as written

explanation.surface: A short instruction to recommend having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: ADVOCATE cut short is ADVOCAT, and A goes inside it before the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocaat is a Dutch liqueur made from eggs, sugar and brandy, so it is one kind of drink.

clue.text: Change the last Word document's header

parts.note: amen is said as the final word of a prayer

indicators.note: a header is at the top, so only the opening letter of that word is used

parts.note: first letter of document

explanation.surface: Editing the top of the final version of a Microsoft Word file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Word' with a capital suggests the software, but the last word of a prayer or hymn is the point.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to alter or revise something, especially a text, which is to change it.

clue.text: Picked up method, but badly, for part of cheese-making kit

indicators.note: picked up as in heard, so the word for method is taken by its sound

parts.note: a way is a method

indicators.note: badly means done poorly, so the short word before it is muddled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone learnt a cheese-making method badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Whey is the watery liquid separated from curds, and a whey tub is the vessel that collects it.

clue.text: Leader of Tories making cuts, which is difficult

indicators.note: the leader is at the front, so only the opening letter of that word is used

parts.note: first letter of Tories
axing means cutting

explanation.surface: The Conservative leader is slashing budgets, which is a hard job.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a tax pun on a Tory budget; Tories are Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxing means demanding and burdensome, making heavy demands on someone, so hard or difficult.

clue.text: British scoundrel, it's said

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a rogue is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: Supposedly there is a British villain about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' looks like a sound signal, but it defines the answer: an accent is something spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a regional accent, especially an Irish one, which is the way speech is pronounced.

clue.text: Left article with disappointing news for Jeremy Clarkson?

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
an is the indefinite article
a downer is something depressing

explanation.surface: Clarkson, famous for a farm TV show, receiving more bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Clarkson, the TV presenter, owns a farm in the Cotswolds shown in Clarkson's Farm; the question mark flags him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarkson owns a farm, so he is one example of someone who owns property and acres.

clue.text: Wealthy individual to take over Barclays, initially

parts.note: to nab is to grab
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the bank is used

parts.note: first letter of Barclays

explanation.surface: A rich tycoon plans to take over Barclays bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a person of great wealth, originally one who made a fortune in India.

clue.text: King claiming the French become more friendly

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the word for king grips the French article

parts.note: rex is Latin for king
la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: A monarch claiming France then warms to its people.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax is to loosen up and become less formal or tense, so to become more friendly.

clue.text: Cover head in outdoor pool

parts.note: a lid is a cover

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of outdoor

explanation.surface: Advice to cover your head at the open-air swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming bath, which is a kind of pool for swimmers.

clue.text: Fresh support system

definitions.meaning: first meaning: invigorating, as cold air
second meaning: a framework of braces

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a new support network; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracing air is cool and invigorating, while bracing is also the set of struts or braces holding a structure up.

clue.text: Crazy about North American pop star

parts.note: mad means crazy
on means about, concerning
NA is the abbreviation for North American

explanation.surface: A fan wild about an American singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container signal but here simply gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Madonna is the American singer known as the Queen of Pop, a famous chart act since the 1980s.

clue.text: Upper-class girl finally treated terrible gas — about time!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the gas goes round the abbreviation for time
finally points to the closing letter of each of the two words after it

parts.note: last letter of treated
last letter of terrible
butane is a fuel gas
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A posh girl at last gets treatment for her dreadful wind, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible gas' looks like an anagram, but terrible only lends its last letter alongside treated.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young upper-class woman making her first formal entrance into society.
